title: Plans, elevations & nets
examples: How do I know which view is the front?
Can I find the net for something curved?
What is the difference between a plan and an elevation?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how to draw views of 3D shapes. We will learn about plans and elevations.
A plan shows what the shape looks like when you look down on it. Imagine looking at a box from above. That view is the plan.
An elevation shows one flat side view of the object. You can draw a front view, a side view, or a back view. These are elevations.
A net is a flat pattern that can be folded to make a 3D shape. Think of the cardboard you cut out to make a box.

draw.text: Net: Flat pattern for a solid

explain.say: Let us look at a simple cube. Its plan will be a square. Its front elevation will also be a square.

faq.q: What is the difference between a plan and an elevation?
faq.a: The plan is what you see when you look down onto the object from above. An elevation is what you see looking straight at one of the sides.
asks: Is the plan the same as the front view?

faq.q: How many views do I need to draw for a shape?
faq.a: Usually, you need at least three views: the plan, the front elevation, and the side elevation. This gives a complete picture.
asks: Do I need to draw all sides?

faq.q: What is a net, and why do we use it?
faq.a: A net is the 2D shape that folds up to create the 3D object. We use it to see if the shape can be built from flat pieces.
asks: Can I make a box from a net?

faq.q: If the object is a cylinder, what will the plan look like?
faq.a: The plan view of a cylinder will be a circle. The front elevation will be a rectangle showing the height and diameter.
asks: What is the top view of a can?
What shape is the plan for a cylinder?

faq.q: Do I have to draw all the lines on the net?
faq.a: Yes, you must draw all the edges of the net. These lines show where the pieces connect when folded up.
asks: Are the lines on the net important?
What do the lines mean on the net?

facts: The plan view shows the shape as if viewed from directly above.
An elevation shows the height and width of one side of the object.
A net is a two-dimensional pattern that forms a three-dimensional solid.
For simple rectangular prisms, the plan and the front elevation are often the same shape.

quiz.say: If you look at a rectangular block from above, what view are you drawing?
quiz.why: The plan view is always the view you see when looking straight down onto the object.

wrong.0: A net is the flat pattern, not the view itself.
wrong.1: A cross-section is what you see when you cut through the middle.
wrong.3: Elevation refers to looking at the side or front, not from above.

quiz.say: What shape will the net of a square-based pyramid look like?

options.show: One square base with four triangles attached
options.say: One square base with four triangles attached

quiz.why: The net must include the base and all the triangular faces that fold up to meet at the apex.

wrong.0: This only gives you the base and misses the sides.
wrong.1: This shape does not account for the sloping sides meeting at a point.
wrong.2: The pyramid has triangles, not just squares.

quiz.say: If the front elevation is a triangle, what must the plan view be?
quiz.why: The plan view is the projection onto the floor; a triangle viewed from above looks like a line segment.

wrong.0: This would mean the object has width from above, which is not true for a simple triangle.
wrong.1: A point means there is no width or length at all.
wrong.2: A rectangle implies the object has constant width throughout its length.
